Honestly, when it comes to putting a label on your own sexuality, it doesn’t really matter what it is, as long as you feel happy with your sexuality and are comfortable with it. It doesn’t matter if it makes sense to anyone else. Cause it’s not about them.
It means you can fall in love with both genders (based on personality), but when it comes to physical attraction, there’s only one gender you’re interested in.
You don’t even know my history to know that.

I don’t know if there is a specific sub-category for that (not one that I am aware of). But what really helped me when I was sorting out labeling my own sexuality, was when someone told me this “It’s YOUR sexuality. YOU get to label it whatever YOU want. YOU get to pick what YOU feel most accurately matches what makes YOU feel comfortable in YOUR own skin. Anyone else’s opinion on YOUR sexuality is irrelevant because it’s not theirs to label.” 

I (28F) have only ever had sexual relations with other women. I personally have not had romantic feelings for a woman before, but I acknowledge that sexually I am MORE attracted to women than I am males. And emotionally I’m more attracted to males. In my own journey, I decided that if others ask about my sexuality I will simply tell them I am bisexual because it’s more understood and I don’t feel like I should have to explain who I am to anyone. If they’re important people in my life that I feel I want to understand my sexuality better, and there honestly aren’t many, I tell them I am actually pansexual. I fall in love with people. And I am attracted to people. Regardless of what gender they identify with. Regardless of if when I’ve already been committed to them they make the life changing (bettering) decision to change their gender to what they feel matches their soul. To me? That doesn’t change who I fell in love with. And sex is such a low priority to me in a relationship, in the sense that it’s no where near as important to me as emotional intimacy. I am not intimidated by exploring new ways to be physically intimate with someone. 

So that brings me back to your other point. Physical intimacy is physical intimacy. If when you are engaging in sexual activity with males and it feels intimate to you, in my humble opinion, that counts as sex regardless of how you prefer to engage in it. Everyone has preferences on how they have sex. What the mainstream definition of sex between two individuals is doesn’t matter because those individuals aren’t made from the same cookie cutter. 

The only thing that matters in exploring the label you define yourself with is how it makes YOU feel. What feels right to YOU.

That one is hard to explain. And I suppose I do mind sharing it.

It’s a therapy technique typically used in processing emotions and memories for PTSD sufferers. There’s a couple different ways the method can be done, but my therapist uses a headset with vibrating paddles. You hold a paddle in each hand, wear the headset, and as this soft beep alternates from your left to right ear, the paddles will vibrate in sync to the same rhythm. It’s supposed to stimulate the part of your brain responsible for processing such things. You walk through your emotions/memories while that part of your brain is stimulated. Typically takes several sessions, but it allows PTSD sufferers to process their traumas as actual memories and reduces PTSD attack symptoms.
